summary: Vladimir Tikhonov works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at St. Petersburg University, Korea University, and under Kwang Cho, Chul-hwan Chung, and Mikhail Nikolaevich Pak, becoming a professor at the University of Oslo around 2000.

Vladimir Vyacheslavovich Balabushevich was an indologist and historian. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, attested in 1970 and 1990.
Volkbert Näther is an indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Marburg (attested 1975), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Claus Vogel.

Volker Caumanns is a Tibetologist who earned an MA under David P. Jackson at the University of Hamburg and a PhD under Franz-Karl Ehrhard at LMU Munich. He held posts at Munich, Lumbini International Research Institute, and Bern.

Volker Grabowsky specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Kiel, he held positions at the University of Passau, University of Hamburg, National University of Laos, and University of Münster.
W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963), H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.
W. H. D. Rouse was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his education at Cheltenham College and Christ's College, Cambridge around 1882 to 1886.

W. H. R. Rivers studied at Tonbridge School, Barts and The London School of Medicine, University of London, and St John's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Cambridge (circa 1893–1922) and University College London (circa 1897–1900).

W. Norman Brown worked in Indology and history. He studied at Hiram College, Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, and with Franklin Edgerton, later serving as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1969–1973).

W. Randolph Kloetzli earned a PhD at the University of Chicago in 1964 and studied under teachers including Paul Tillich and Mircea Eliade. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunaratne was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Dharmaraja College, Ananda College, University of Ceylon, and SOAS University of London. He was Dean of the Faculty of Oriental Studies at Ceylon (1952–1973).

W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and served as professor and Department Chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ceylon under G. P. Malalasekera, Calcutta, and Paris under Paul Demiéville. He held an academic post at the University of Oxford from circa 1974 to 1977.

Walter Eugene Clark was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1923–1927) and Harvard University as Wales Professor of Sanskrit (1927–1950).
Walter Ewer was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Fort William College around 1801 to 1803 and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1801 to 1839.

Walter Liebenthal was a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology. He held positions at the University of Paris, Visva-Bharati University (around 1952–1959), and the University of Tübingen (around 1960–1965).

Walter M. Spink worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Amherst College, he held posts at Brandeis University (~1956–1961) and served as Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2005).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Otto Franke, taught there from 1926 to 1934, and subsequently held posts at the University of London and SOAS (circa 1938–1960).
Walter Slaje is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna from around 1974 to 1979. He served as a professor at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1999 to 2020.
